text:
Priya: Heads-up — spike planning for capacity-constrained regions. Proposal: add 'lanes' to route matching and a soft-fallback lane that routes to smaller/quantized models when primary QPS > threshold. Thoughts?

Mika: can you sketch the config you have in mind?

Priya: sure, rough YAML:```yaml
route: /v1/generate
match: path_prefix: /v1/generate
lanes:
  - name: primary
    models: [open-30b, rwd-64b]
    cb_trigger: util>0.95 for 30s
  - name: degraded
    models: [open-7b-q4, rwd-13b-q4]
    warm_kv: true
  - name: fallback
    models: [open-3b-q8]
    max_hops: 2
quota_attr: preserve_origin: true
headers:
  priority_header: x-rwd-priority
  fallback_trace: x-rwd-fallback-path
```

Jorge: we should allow clients to set `x-rwd-priority` for enterprise keys only (so startups can't spoof). Also prefer header override over path rules when set.

Sam: telemetry asks: add `fallback_reason` tag and record token_cost delta per-request so we can measure economics of fallback.

Eve: console UX idea — surface per-route SLO + a "simulate fallback" button that runs a dry-run and shows expected model, latency/cost delta.

infra-bot: CB alert: circuit-breaker tripped on gpu-pool-11 (us-west-2) at 2026-03-15T14:03Z for route /v1/generate primary lane.

Mika: if CB trips, do we warm backup KV caches? switching cold causes big latency spikes.

Priya: plan is to keep standby warm_kv for degraded lane and prefetch top-k for active sessions during transitions. Also do gradual fanout: 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 30s to avoid thundering.

Sam: add monitoring panels for `fallback_latency_p50/p95/p99` and `lane_switch_rate`. Alert if fallback_p99 > baseline + 200ms.

Jorge: billing question — when a request is routed to fallback, whose quota gets consumed? fallback model's quota or original route's quota?

Priya: default: preserve original quota attribution so customers see consistent billing; provide opt-in header `x-rwd-bill-to-fallback: true` for those who want accurate per-model billing. Document in API reference.

Eve: also show billing attribution in the call detail inspector and add a short explainer flyout in the rollout UI.

Mika: edge case: multi-hop cascades A->B->C cause oscillation. Enforce `max_hops=2` and `circuit_suppress=true` to prevent re-entering a previously failed lane. Example inline: `if hops>max_hops then drop_to_fallback`.

Priya: :thumbsup: I'll update the RFC with those rules and simulation plan. Adding unit tests for hop limits and billing behavior. Can someone create the dashboard + example traces? @Sam @Eve

Sam: on it — will add a lane-switch heatmap, fallback_reason breakdown, and a trace panel that highlights `x-rwd-fallback-path`.

Jorge: I'll gate the header override change behind enterprise token check and add a small migration script to backfill existing tokens.

deploy-bot: Deploy scheduled: feature-flag `route-lanes` -> canary 5% at 2026-03-16T02:00Z (rolling 20m).

Priya: Follow-up: add `x-rwd-fallback-path` to logs with comma-separated steps (e.g., primary,degraded,fallback) and `x-rwd-fallback-reason` (e.g., cb,quota,latency). Helps replay.

Mika: perfect. also add a `simulated_fallback` toggle in console so product/CS can test without billing impact.

Eve: I'll wire the simulate button to create a synthetic trace and show cost delta overlay.

Priya: thanks all — will PR the RFC and mark for review.
